nia: quick sync — runtime wants a compact handoff token so probe hints can survive canaries without allowing unsafe route swaps. thoughts?

peter: +1. we need a tiny header on compiled policies that runtimes can check before applying hints. call it a shape_tag + compat_bitmap.

olga: agree but prefer different names to avoid confusion with existing fields: shape_tag (monotonic int), shape_sig (short hex), feature_bits (list). runtimes only accept hints when shape_tag in {current, current-1}.

rachel: also add a tiny "binding_map" when nodes are renamed during a non-additive change: old_path->new_path. if binding_map is present, runtimes can translate hints. if map too large (>150 entries) require manual rollout.

peter: for the hint token we propose: token = xxh64(shape_sig || node_path || delta || runtime_epoch). attach confidence float and a namespace "probe-<runtime-id>". keep token size ~8 bytes.

nia: should compiler emit a per-artifact index mapping node_path -> compact id (4 bytes) to speed verification?

olga: yes. runtime verifier can then do a constant-time check: lookup compact id, compare proof hash. if mismatch or ambiguity -> reject and route to compiled default. increment metric policy.hint.reject.

rachel: GC rules: runtimes keep keys for current shape_tag and previous only. keys older than that are GC candidates unless artifact declares "cross-accept" bit. default canary window 30m.

peter: one more: require the compiler to avoid reusing node_ids across non-consecutive shape_tags. CI lint should catch that.

nia: security note: tokens must never include secrets. only deterministic hashes.

olga: tradeoffs: 8 bytes per token is cheap but collisions possible; we accept probabilistic collisions because fallback is safe. document that.

rachel: operational checklist: 1) compiler: emit shape_tag/shape_sig/feature_bits + optional binding_map + compact index. 2) runtime: namespace keys by (shape_tag, namespace, runtime_id), attach token+confidence, scrub older keys. 3) policy-service: synchronous lightweight verify of token -> accept advisory or reject; async deep-validate and alert on surprises.

nia: I'll write a short RFC with examples for two policy flavors (latency-leaning and cost-leaning) showing accepted and rejected hint flows. ping me for review.

signals-bot: canary:policy-compiler v2.6 deployed -> canary 8% :white_check_mark: <https://ci/redwood/882211>

peter: thanks — let's land CI lints and a tiny verifier prototype before next canary ramp.
